hero.title: The Local-First Peer-to-Peer Stack
hero.subtitle: No servers. No accounts. No passwords. Your data lives on your device and travels directly to the people you share it with. Networks run with always-on peers or entirely without them — add one whenever a group wants more reach, and when none is reachable, devices connect directly by scanning a code. Neither mode is the fallback.

stack.title: The five layers
stack.sub: Every layer works without a central service — and every layer is an open-source building block you can use on its own.

identity.name: Identity
identity.desc: WebAuthn / Passkeys / DIDs and Web3 wallets — your keys, your browser

data.name: Data
data.desc: OrbitDB — CRDT-based, so concurrent edits merge instead of colliding; your data stays on your device

sync.name: Sync
sync.desc: libp2p — direct browser-to-browser connections across NATs, through relay nodes or free and out of band with a scanned code or an invite link

infra.name: Infrastructure
infra.desc: Relay Button — on-demand relays on decentralized compute, sponsorable by anyone

archive.name: Archive
archive.desc: Filecoin / Aleph IPFS — decentralised storage for backups that outlive devices

projects.title: Projects
projects.sub: Demos and prototypes, not slideware — each project is a building block of the stack with demo, source, and packages.

usecases.title: Use cases
usecases.sub: Standalone projects grow out of the stack. Each has a short pitch deck — as a page to link and as a PDF to forward.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.sub: Common questions about local-first, encryption, metadata and infrastructure — answered honestly, including what isn't finished yet.
